name: Connected Earth Museum
tagline: Walk a 3D virtual museum where each painting opens a live NASA data visualization of how Earth's systems connect.
problem: The links between temperature, fires, population, emissions and air quality are hard for the public to see in separate datasets.
solution: A React/three.js museum modelled in Blender: a guide character leads visitors along a spline path; clicking paintings opens a 3D globe with time series (land and ocean temperature, vegetation, emissions, population, wildfires), 2D maps linking fire hotspots, precipitation and wind, and population with emissions and real-time air quality, ending with a quiz mini-game.
demo_moment: Team-described: step into a painting and land inside a data visualization of the planet.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for most effectively combining technical and creative skills.
An immersive virtual museum where an AI host guides users through 3D and 2D visualizations of temperature, population density, wildfires and more.
Built its own museum model, baked lighting and a path spline editor rather than using a template.
A museum is a format everyone understands, so the data exploration needs no instructions — the art award rewards that pairing of craft and data.

lessons: Put data inside a familiar place (a museum) so exploring it feels natural.
Craft visible in 3D assets counts as depth for an art-and-technology award.
LATAM precedent: a student team from Brazil won Art & Technology.

sources.note: Team-written tour, visualizations, technical details, AI-use disclosure (ChatGPT, DALL-E for slides, ElevenLabs guide voice), data list.
